en: Project manager: tasks without an owner
Hello {manager}, {no_owner} tasks on {name} have no owner. Please assign them this week so that the look-ahead is complete.
Hello {approved_by}, version {version} of the baseline of {project} waits for your approval. The new end is {end}. Reason: {reason}.
Project manager: float below the limit
Hello {manager}, the float of {name} on {project} is {float_days} days ({state}). Watch owner: {watch}. Please check its links and the people on it.
Hello {manager}, this week on {name}: {week_start} tasks start and {week_due} are due, and {late_n} are overdue. Next milestone: {next_ms}. Please confirm the owners by Monday noon.
Project manager: fixed date at risk
Hello {manager}, the fixed date {name} on {project} is {date} and the forecast is {forecast}: {margin} spare days ({state}). Please plan the recovery before a penalty applies.
PMO lead: schedule variance this week
Hello, schedule variance on {name}: forecast end {forecast_end} against baseline {end}, {slip} days ({sched}). Manager: {manager}. We review it at the weekly meeting.
Hello, the recovery action for {name} on {project} was due on {due} and is still {status}. Cause: {cause}. Owner: {owner}. Please chase it.
Hello, the week of {start} holds {due_n} due tasks and {hours} planned hours against {capacity} hours of capacity (load {load}). {away} people are away. Please help to level the week.
Hello {sponsor}, the milestone {name} on {project} moved from {planned} to {forecast}. We will tell you the effect on the end date this week.
Hello {sponsor}, the new forecast end of {name} is {forecast_end}. The baseline end is {end}, so the slip is {slip} days. A recovery plan follows.
Hello {sponsor}, the delay on {name} ({project}) comes from: {cause}. Our recovery action is: {action}, due {due}. The recovery plan is attached.
Sponsor: approval needed for the plan
Hello {sponsor}, we need your decision this week to hold {name} on {date} ({project}). The forecast is {forecast}, with {margin} spare days. Penalty per week late: {penalty_week}.
Hello {contact}, the milestone {name} of {project} is planned for {forecast} (baseline {planned}). Please keep your reviewers free in that week.
Client contact: your input is needed
Hello {who}, we still need {item} for {project} by {needed_by}. We asked on {asked_on}. Please tell us when we will receive it.
Hello {contact}, the release {release} is planned for {date}. The code freeze starts on {freeze}. Please confirm the window and who signs off on your side.
Client contact: change to the schedule
Hello {contact}, we moved the end of {name} on {project} from {old_end} to {new_end}. The reason is: {reason}. Please tell us if this affects your plans.
Hello {contact}, our next company closure is on {next_closure}. The plan for {name} already skips it. Please tell us about your own closure days.
Hello {who}, please confirm the delivery date of {item} for {project}. We need it by {needed_by}.
Vendor: delivery is late, new date
Hello {who}, {item} for {project} was needed by {needed_by} and we have waited {days_waiting} days. Please send the new date today.
Hello {who}, please confirm your booking dates for {item} on {project}. We asked on {asked_on}. Our owner is {owner}.

The baseline runs from {col:projects.start} to {col:projects.end}. The forecast end is {col:projects.forecast_end}, which is {col:projects.slip} days against the baseline. The schedule colour is: {col:projects.sched}.
Each phase shows its forecast end and the share of its work done.

The plan holds {col:projects.tasks_n} tasks. {col:projects.done_n} are done and {col:projects.late_n} are overdue. Work done, weighted by hours: {col:projects.pct_done}. Hours left: {col:projects.hours_left}.

The schedule skips weekends and company holidays. The next company closure is on {col:projects.next_closure}. A change of a date is entered on the Schedule Changes sheet and approved by the sponsor or the PMO lead.

Baseline date: {col:milestones.planned}. Forecast date: {col:milestones.forecast}. Actual date: {col:milestones.actual}. Slip: {col:milestones.slip} days. The date check shows: {col:milestones.check}.
A milestone is met when it is reached on or before its baseline date. A milestone that moves is reported to the sponsor and the client contact with the reason and the new date.

Baseline start: {col:baselines.start}. Baseline end: {col:baselines.end}. Duration: {col:baselines.duration} days. Change against the version before: {col:baselines.change}. End moved: {col:baselines.moved} days.
After approval the baseline does not change. A new version is made only for an approved change, and the earlier version stays on record.
Schedule change notice to the client
We moved the end of the task {col:changes.name} from {col:changes.old_end} to {col:changes.new_end}. That is {col:changes.shift} days, or {col:changes.wshift} working days.
The reason is: {col:changes.reason}. {col:changes.approved_by} approved the change on {col:changes.date}.
Please tell us within three working days if this change affects your plans or the dates you are waiting for. If we do not hear from you, the new date stands.
The task {col:delays.name} is {col:delays.days_late} days late. We raised the delay on {col:delays.raised}.
Our recovery action is: {col:delays.action}. Owner: {col:delays.owner}. Due on {col:delays.due}. Status: {col:delays.status}.
Where the cause is outside the team we ask for your support. We will report again when the action is done.

Week starting {col:lookahead.start}. Tasks starting: {col:lookahead.starting}. Tasks due: {col:lookahead.due_n}. Hours planned: {col:lookahead.hours}. Late tasks: {col:lookahead.late_n}. People away: {col:lookahead.away}.
Tasks due in the next three weeks: {col:lookahead.due_w2}, {col:lookahead.due_w3} and {col:lookahead.due_w4}. Hours planned: {col:lookahead.hrs_w2}, {col:lookahead.hrs_w3} and {col:lookahead.hrs_w4}.
Team capacity this week: {col:lookahead.capacity} hours. Load: {col:lookahead.load}, so the week is: {col:lookahead.state}. Holidays in the week: {col:lookahead.holidays_n}.
Owners confirm their tasks on Monday. A heavy week is levelled before it starts.
Task: {col:critical.name} on {col:critical.project}. Task status: {col:critical.task_status}. Days late: {col:critical.days_late}.
Float: {col:critical.float_days} days. The limit in our settings is {set:float_limit} days, so the state is: {col:critical.state}. The driver is: {col:critical.driver}.
Watch owner: {col:critical.watch}. Action: {col:critical.action}. Due on {col:critical.due}. Action state: {col:critical.action_state}.
Every critical item is reviewed on Monday. An item with little float needs a recovery action with an owner and a date.

The code freeze starts on {col:releases.freeze}, {set:freeze_days} working days before the release. Days to go: {col:releases.days_to}. State: {col:releases.state}. Window check: {col:releases.window}.
Client contact: {col:releases.contact}. Before the release the owner confirms the freeze, the test result, the way back and the people on call. The client contact confirms the window in writing.
Recovery plan for a late project

The baseline end is {col:projects.end} and the forecast end is {col:projects.forecast_end}. The slip is {col:projects.slip} days, or {col:projects.slip_pct} of the baseline duration. The schedule colour is: {col:projects.sched}.

Hours left: {col:projects.hours_left}. To hold the baseline end the team needs about {col:projects.catch_hours} more hours each week. Overdue tasks: {col:projects.late_n}. Tasks without an owner: {col:projects.no_owner}.

Recovery steps: put more people on the late tasks, start work in parallel where the links allow it, move or cut scope that the sponsor agrees to give up, and remove blockers with the client contact. Each step has an owner and a date.
We review the plan every week until the forecast end is back on the baseline or a new baseline is approved.

Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: warning days, float limit, schedule colours, focus share and the days of code freeze.
List your projects on Projects and your people on Team. Baseline end, forecast end, manager and sponsor sit on the project row; slip and colour fill in.
Break each project into phases and work packages on Work Breakdown, then list the tasks on Task List with owner, dates, estimated hours, percent done and status.
Link tasks on Dependencies with a link type and a lag. The check column finds missing, circular and conflicting links before they hurt the plan.
Enter company holidays on Holidays and leave on Leave Calendar. Working Days shows the working days and team hours of each month and every end date skips closure days.
Set milestones, fixed dates and releases on Milestones, Fixed Dates and Releases. Slip, spare days, freeze dates and window checks fill in.
Keep each approved plan on Baselines and the dates of every phase on Phase Plan. Log every moved date on Schedule Changes and every late task on Delay Register.
Use Three-point Estimates before you commit to hours and Estimate Accuracy after tasks finish, so the next estimate starts from your own history.
Every Monday read Look-ahead and Critical Items: heavy weeks, people away, tasks with little float and the action and owner for each one.
Use the 14 calculators for end dates, working days, estimates, duration, float, buffer, delay impact, forecast end, catch-up, shifts, release windows, approvals and delay cost.
Print 10 sheets and 9 documents, follow 9 checklists and tap a message link to open your messaging app with the text ready.
Read Schedule Dashboard and Charts every week and send the sponsor note before dates move, not after.
Plan team capacity, timesheets, leave and utilisation for every project
Plan who is free, who is overloaded and where the hours go
Weekly capacity with leave and closures
for every person and week the contract hours less company closure days and approved leave give the hours really available, set against the hours allocated
Load check: over, full, balanced or free
each person's allocation on all projects is checked against your own limits, so overload and free time show before they hurt a project
Allocation sheet with hours per week
person, project, share of the week and dates become hours per week, a state and the phone of the project manager
every person and week is shown as approved, waiting, returned or missing, with the due date and the days late
Utilisation by month against each person's target
capacity, hours logged and billable hours are compared with the target of the person and marked above, on or below target
Skills matrix with project skill gaps
skill levels of the team are matched to what each project needs and the gap in people is counted, so a missing skill is seen early
working days without closure days, days in the next 30 and a warning when the person who covers is away on the same dates
Contractor timesheets with an invoice check
hours worked are compared with hours invoiced for every contractor week, and rate times hours gives the cost to pay
Contractor bookings with cost so far
hours per week times weeks times rate gives the planned cost, next to the hours and cost so far and a warning before a booking ends
Resource gaps turned into full-time posts
missing hours per week become full-time posts, with the days a request has been open and a check of the start date
Rate card with the latest rates and margin
cost rate and charge rate of each role over time, the margin per hour and which rate is current today
Overtime log with the cost of the premium
overtime hours, reason and approval with the cost including the premium, so extra hours are agreed and priced
